asker_query: Sister, I want to prepare for my last days — I will not go to ICU, I will stay at home, I have to prepare some papers for my wife, I have things to say to my son. But whenever I raise the topic, my wife cries, my son stops me saying 'don't talk like this'. How can you help me?
answer:
Address the patient’s autonomy and family dynamics: Acknowledge his right to prepare for end-of-life wishes while addressing family collusion (withholding information to "protect" him). Use empathetic communication: “We understand this is difficult, but sharing your plans can help your family feel supported, not abandoned” (similar to IndianPrimer’s approach to realistic hope). Encourage family inclusion with a home care team to simplify care and clarify prognosis, reducing uncertainty (Twycross emphasizes anticipatory guidance). For family resistance, reference the IndianPrimer’s note on collusion: “Families may avoid discussions to protect you, but open dialogue ensures your wishes are honored.” Reassure: “We’ll support your choice to stay home and assist with paperwork/communication with your son.”
